title: Frontend's "Help with commodity codes" gives one sentence and no way to look a code up; Design release 1 explains what a commodity code is and links out to the Trade Tariff tool.

finding.frontend: Opening the "Help with commodity codes" details reveals a single sentence — "Commodity codes are used to classify goods for import and export." — and nothing else. It is passed to the govukDetails macro as plain text, so it cannot carry a link (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/search.njk:31-34, with the string at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:9). A user who does not know their commodity code is told what one is and left with no way to find it.
finding.prototype: The details of the same name, in the same position on the page, holds three paragraphs: "Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers.", "A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods.", and "You can look up commodity codes using the Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab).", where "Trade Tariff tool" is a link to https://www.gov.uk/trade-tariff opening in a new tab (app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:119-132).
finding.difference: Replace the one-sentence help text with Design release 1's three paragraphs, including the Trade Tariff link and its "(opens in a new tab)" suffix. That means passing HTML to the details rather than text, so the copy entry changes shape as well as wording; the Welsh copy file beside it carries the same single string and needs the same treatment. Nothing has to land first — the link is a public GOV.UK page.
finding.falsifiedBy: A link out to the Trade Tariff tool, or any other commodity-code lookup, reachable from the frontend's commodity page. The captured DOM for fe-commodity-search contains exactly one link inside the main content — "Cancel and return to hub" — and no commodity-code lookup anywhere in the frontend's source.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs (capture/html/frontend/fe-commodity-search.html:226-235 and capture/html/prototype/dr1-what-are-you-importing.html) and both 2x page shots. Read the cited source at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/search.njk:31-34, copy.en.js:7-10 and app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:119-132. Ran the falsifier: grepped "Trade Tariff" and "trade-tariff" across src/server on the implementation side — no match. CORRECT.
finding.correction:
The claim stands and the falsifier does not fire; three points of record. (1) The falsifier's supporting sentence said the captured page carries "no external href at all". That is true of the main content and false of the page: the GOV.UK header logo links to https://www.gov.uk/ and the footer carries privacy, cookies, accessibility and Open Government Licence links. The falsifier has been rescoped to the main content, which is what it was always testing, and the substance is unaffected — no commodity-code lookup exists anywhere in the frontend's source. (2) A detail for whoever writes the copy: on the requirements side "(opens in a new tab)" sits outside the anchor, after a
, rather than inside the link text (app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:123-124). (3) One citation was a line out — the govukDetails call is at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/search.njk:31-34, not :32-35 — and the prose now says so.
